summary:
# NOTES: *Adele Doring at Boarding-School* (Grace May North, 1921; ill. Florence Liley Young; Lothrop, Lee & Shepard, Boston)
Series prior: *Adele Doring of the Sunnyside Club*, *Adele Doring on a Ranch*. Dedicated to Sunnyside Club of California.

## CHARACTERS
- **Adele Doring**: 14, 8th grade, rose tam-o'-shanter, rose sweater coat. Heroine, "Della." Mother = "Mumsie"/"Adorable Mother"; father = "Giant Daddy." Brother **Jack** (Dorchester High next year, lazy, handsome). Friend Eva Dearman (Arizona ranch, Uncle Dick Dearman); Amanda Brown (married cowboy "Rusty Pete").
- **Sunny Seven/Six** (Sunnyside Club): **Rosamond "Rosie" Wright** (romantic, short yellow curls, drawls; mother a social butterfly; crush on Bob); **Betty Burd** ("Bettykins," "Little One," youngest, pigtail braids, dimple; uncle **George Burd**, young editor, prosperous, "Puss," "Betty Bobbets"; father dead); **Doris Drexel** (devoted father Mr. Drexel; "Dory"; plays piano); **Peggy Pierce** (mischievous; father owns dry-goods store; "Inseparable" with Doris); **Bertha Angel** ("Burdie," practical, chairman, spectacles, mathematician; father grocer; brother **Bob Angel**, "Bobby-boy"); **Gertrude Willis** ("Trudie," eldest, minister's daughter, older; father a theology grad; mother ex-high school teacher; sister Ruth; many siblings; 16th birthday during C.E.P.).
- **Carol Lorens**: 15, new Sunnysider from Chicago suburb. Father lawyer (lost fortune); mother (Mummie); brother **Peter** (law student); twins **David** and **Dorothy** (7). Lives in brown farmhouse on Lake Road in apple orchard (father's boyhood home). Grandpa Lorens; great-grandfather refused English royal title. Carol gets Evelyn's companion job. Carol plays Norah in the play.
- **Mr. & Mrs. Lorens** (father's words: "What would my mother do?").
- **Mr. Dartmoor**: rich old client, castle-like estate near Lorens home; lions on steps; shaggy grey brows, blue twinkling eyes; cane; called "ogre" by twins; "Santa Claus" per David. Once "pals" with Carol's grandfather.
- **Evelyn Dartmoor**: 15, granddaughter, tall, slender, black dress; collie in portrait; lonely; parents dead; mother left her weeks before.
- **Mr. Dickerson**: Sunnyside principal. **Miss Donovan**: 8th-grade teacher, left to care for elderly mother.
- **Madame Deriby**: Linden Hall matron; tall, stately, silvery hair, grey eyes, kind.
- **Miss Sharpleigh** (teacher, sorts mail); **Miss Merritt** (youngest teacher, drills curtsies); **Miss Berry** (kindergarten; brother ill); **Miss Perring** (uniform maker); **Madame Vandeheuton** (French essay medal); **Professor Patz** (Doris's piano).
- **Mr. Drakely**: postman (Sunnyside). **Uncle Danny**: deaf station-master, Sunnyside. **Granny Dorset**: cottage on Cherry Lane.
- **Patrick O'Neil**, **Billie/Bill**: Linden gardeners/stable boys; Patrick drives bus with two white horses; Irish brogue.
- **Anne**: small girl messenger.
- **Dick Jensen**: 15, candy-shop boy; **Jolly Pirates** = boys' club (Jack, Bob, Dick, Donald).
- **Gladys Merle Jones**: "Lady" clique leader; father Beef King, Chicago (actually uneducated Buffalo ranchman, "Mr. Jones," red-faced, stout). Clique: **Anita Ryan** (echoes Gladys; aunt Laura near Sunnyside), **Janet Nagel** (defects to Carol), **Jenny Clark**. Gladys reforms.
- **Mr. Haley**: riding-master. **Mr. O'Rourke**: farmer (eggs, butter, turkeys, sleigh/wagon).
- **Elmhurst** (Ellsworth estate, ~10 yrs unoccupied): **Mr. A. R. Ellsworth** (deceased; stern portrait, shaggy brows). **Arthur Ellsworth** (~18, handsome lad, tally-ho, tally-ho driver, likes Gertrude). **Louise Ellsworth** ("Aunt Louise," pale, beautiful, Alise's aunt). **Mrs. Diggitt** (lodge-house); **Mr. Diggitt** (head gardener, "flowers are like children").
- **Alise Alderly**: golden-haired, 6, orphan; mother = Louise's sister (married against stern father). Calls Gertrude "big sister." Birthday party at Elmhurst.
- **Katrina Mason**: spoiled rich girl, fretful, "Iceland" = her room (west wing). Taming via Carol's "loving kindness"; shares Thanksgiving box.
- **Marie Le Clerc**: French essay medal winner.
- **Evelyn's grandfather** (Mr. Dartmoor).
- **Matilda Perkins → "Starr"** (double-r): 15, Dakota prairie girl, Bishop Wesley's protégée; mother Margaret Inslay (English-born, Ivondale); brothers **Basil** (handsome, herds cattle) and **Cedric** (oldest, plows); dog **Shep**; wears plaid shawl, beaver cap, thick woolen mittens; wonderful brown eyes.
- **Geraldine Barrington**: "Lady Stuckup," English haughty roommate (Barrington Manor); father Mr. Barrington (traveling West seeking sister); Geraldine's cousin Starr = Matilda's mother's family.
- **Nina Best**: former cupola-room occupant (Peggy's fake ghost story).
- **Madge Petersen**: Dorchester lady, Lady of the Cabin; **Everett Petersen**: her brother, sailor, capsized on Little Bear Lake ("drowned white rat"); "Weeds grow rapidly."
- **Donald Burnley**: Adele's admirer (initials D. B.); Adele hopes for Arizona cattleman.
- **Eva Dearman**: Arizona friend, arrives for C.E.P.
- **Uncle Jack and Aunt Dahlia**: own island in St. Lawrence River (loan for August camping).

## PLACES
Sunnyside (village; Lake Road; Cherry Lane; meadows; elm-tree meeting place; Secret Sanctum log cabin). Dorchester (city; high school). Buffalo (city; 2 hrs train; Gladys's father's business; theater). Linden (station, village; 1 hr local). Linden Hall Seminary (colonial mansion, elm drive, gardens, orchard, cupola, south/west/east/north wings, Apple-Blossom Alley = corridor with apple-blossom wallpaper, recreation hall, dining-room, library, gym, Madame Deriby's office, "Den"). Little Bear Lake. Elmhurst (iron gates, lodge, ivy wall, marble statue of a girl, pedestal name). Dakota prairie (Matilda's home; sod house; Silver Creek is Arizona).

## EVENTS (in order)
**Ch1**: Adele at library mirror; rides to school with Rosie; meets Carol (new). Carol must attend Dorchester High (too advanced). Carol's family moved after financial loss; twins in apple trees.
**Ch2**: Carol to Mrs. Lorens about school; Mrs. Lorens: Peter gave up college; Carol wanted boarding-school for music and drawing. Carol delivers papers to Mr. Dartmoor (lions, fountain, serving-man). Learns of Evelyn (portrait; at school near Buffalo). Carol cries; Mrs. Lorens: "Don't let's worry..."
**Ch3**: Evelyn's letter to Granddad (lonely; roommate insisted by Madame Deriby). Mr. Dartmoor visits Lorens home; offers Carol place at Linden Hall as Evelyn's companion. Dorothy offers to help mother. Sunny Seven farewell; Adele: "Queer things happen."
**Ch4**: Carol departs on 9:00 train; Carol's father advice. Dartmoor carriage. Sunnysiders at station. Carol meets Evelyn at Linden station. School bus; Linden Hall described.
**Ch5**: Carol's letter read by Adele (Madame Deriby, room yellow, forty pupils). Miss Donovan leaves; eighth grade closed; girls to Dorchester; Mr. Dickerson. Secret Sanctum meeting: five plan Linden Hall; Betty can't (Uncle George); Gertrude stays to tutor Betty.
**Ch6**: Betty's ride; Uncle George promises to send Betty ("Pet"). Madame Deriby letter (room for eight; new wing; school bus Saturday at four). Girls pack.
**Ch7**: Departure from Sunnyside station; brothers' gifts (Jensen candy boxes, blue-and-gold ribbons); Jack and Bob tease; boys ride to next town.
**Ch8**: Carol & Evelyn in garden; Adele's letter ("Give our love to Evelyn"); bus arrives 4:30. Rooms: Rosie & Bertha; Peggy & Doris (corner gardens); Adele & Betty (corner lake view); Carol & Evelyn move to fourth room. Named Apple-Blossom Alley. Evelyn describes Gladys Merle Jones. Dinner at noon, Miss Sharpleigh; Bertha/Peggy fear snobbery.
**Ch9**: Gladys's clique meets; plan to inquire about Carol's family via Anita's aunt. Gladys & Anita sneak out to mail letter; Patrick & Billie nearly catch them; Billie: "Huh! Nothin' but girls."
**Ch10**: Rain; mail-bag; Miss Sharpleigh hands Anita letter; read aloud: Carol is a poor lawyer's daughter, paid companion. Gladys boasts father "handsome and stately." Janet defends Carol, defects. Adele snubs Gladys.
**Ch11**: Gladys learns father visiting; Mr. Jones arrives (red-faced, "Is my gal anywhere handy?"); Gladys hides. Carol visits; tells great-grandfather story; "The Making of Royalty." Gladys apologizes to father; reconciles.
**Ch12**: Madame Deriby interviews girls individually. Kindergarten teacher Miss Berry leaves; Madame asks Adele for helper; Adele proposes Gertrude. Letter sent.
**Ch13**: Saturday; Mr. Willis phones; Gertrude arrives 2 pm; train stuck on siding; Patrick drives bus; Gertrude rescued.
**Ch14**: Gertrude teaches 10 tots; Alise asks "let me love you"; Alise backstory (grandfather refused to see). Ride to Elmhurst with Mr. Haley; marble statue; name "Alise ... Ellsworth."
**Ch15**: Gertrude sees trunk "A. R. Ellsworth." Turkey-order errand with Adele past Mrs. Diggitt's lodge. Library; Arthur (about 18) greets them; Aunt Louise; Alise Alderly; Louise's sister's baby; car to Linden.
**Ch16**: Meeting on Katrina Mason; Madame Deriby's request. Doris's rhyme picks Carol. Carol visits Katrina, offers Norah/summer-girl role; Katrina admits girls dislike her; Carol suggests sharing Thanksgiving goodies.
**Ch17**: Five o'clock visit; Carol's introductions; Gertrude fetched; feast (turkey, cranberry jelly, potato chips, olives, candy, frosted cookies, chocolate cake, grape juice). Rosamond apologizes; Katrina reforms; rehearsals at 4:30.
**Ch18**: Louise Ellsworth invites all to Thanksgiving dinner; chrysanthemums from Arthur with card "At the hour of three / A surprise there will be!" Boys disguised as Russians (Mellowisky etc.): Bob (Rosie identifies by voice), Jack (Adele), Donald Burnley, a fourth boy. Arthur explains: went to school with boys in Dorchester. Betty thinks Arthur likes Gertrude.
**Ch19**: Snow; sleigh-ride party at Elmhurst (48 girls; Alise's birthday). Play: Carol as Norah; Katrina laughs; bouquet of pink carnations. Midwinter exams; Christmas break; Jolly Pirates meet train. Adele's French essay—Marie Le Clerc wins medal; Adele 2nd. Gladys's theater party (Buffalo). March: new pupil coming.
**Ch20**: Peggy describes Matilda; Gertrude brings her; pop-corn; Lady Stuckup roommate; Dakota history; Adele lends uniform; "Starr" name.
**Ch21**: Starr's blizzard story (Bishop rescued). Adele renames her Starr; Gertrude introduces to roommate.
**Ch22**: Geraldine's indignant visit to Madame Deriby; cupola room offered. Geraldine reads Starr's diary. Peggy's ghost story (Nina Best). Starr finds arbutus; Geraldine's ankle; Mr. O'Rourke's wagon.
**Ch23**: Geraldine asks Starr to stay; reveals loneliness/lost aunt. Father Mr. Barrington returns; Starr's mother was his sister Margaret Inslay (Ivondale). Adele invites Starr to Sunnyside.
**Ch24**: C.E.P. (Closing Exercises Party) announced. Adele invites Donald (D.B.); Jack invited by Doris; Bertha switches to inviting Dick Jensen. Gertrude's surprise party planned; Gertrude & Arthur-like romance glimpsed (boy in roadster).
**Ch25**: Pearl fund: Uncle Pierson's $20; Gertrude bought mother a suit & lilac silk dress; Evelyn treasurer. Betty's pink muslin remade by Adele (square neck, lace ruffles, pink fringe sash).
**Ch26**: Adele's Arizona wish; Eva Dearman coming; Amanda's baby (adobe house, Silver Creek); Jack's letter: Uncle Jack's St. Lawrence island, August camping, need chaperone.
**Ch27**: Madge Petersen agreed; brother Everett; arrival of Eva, Madge, Everett; Arthur takes Everett home; cupola guest room.
**Ch28**: Closing party: Rosie's pink rose; Starr's silver star circlet (Geraldine's gift). Hawaiian musicians; Madame Deriby & Madge chat. Gertrude's surprise: birthday song; Betty presents velvet box of "friendship pearls."
**Ch29**: Orchard lantern supper. Arthur proposes courtship; Gertrude agrees to be his "aunt's niece" if he still cares later; declines help until then.
**Ch30**: Farewell, Linden Hall: packing; Starr invites all to prairie; Adele's farewell speech; song "Farewell, Dear Linden Hall." Last lines: Adele "here endeth another chapter"; Betty: "Adele Doring out camping!"
